gap: No result ChatGPT got sorts the makers' 'MagSafe compatible' claims by what the shopper actually gets: Scooch Wingmate cannot charge wirelessly at all with the case on, and says its MagSafe ring does not change that; Decoded's retailer copy says both the back cover and the wallet are MagSafe-compatible but never says whether it charges with the wallet attached; Nomad's folio lists 'MagSafe & Qi2 charging compatible' but doesn't say where the cards sit. Apple's MagSafe Charger page judges a card case by where the cards are, not by the label: remove them or make sure they aren't between the back of the phone and the charger.
standout_why: I compared against Macworld (cited) and the Apple Accessory Design Guidelines (cited). Macworld lists no case with a card holder or wallet in the content we could see, and gives no charging-with-cards statement for any case. ChatGPT drew its 'advise against rear credit-card pockets' line from the Apple guidelines, so the general principle is already cited. Neither page separates the products into 'no wireless at all', 'charges only with the wallet off' and 'charges with cards in', and neither applies Apple's 'not between the back and the charger' test to named cases. I couldn't open WIRED (the fetch tool is blocked there), so I couldn't check it. The ChatGPT answers also contradict each other on Decoded: one says the wallet must be detached to charge, while the retailer copy says both parts are MagSafe-compatible.
decides: It confirms the page's split. Wallet Slayer and Wingmate are cable-only, so they shouldn't be picked for 'still works with MagSafe charging'; Scooch's own FAQ states this for Wingmate. Among the candidates we have, only a folio whose cards sit in the front flap can pass Apple's placement test with cards loaded. Nomad is the likely pick, but I couldn't source the card position from Nomad itself, so the page should say so. Decoded's 'MagSafe compatible on both parts' doesn't answer the question, and its 1.2 m (about 3.9 ft) drop claim is about half of Nomad's 8 ft. Nomad's price has changed: $74 today, down from $99, in a 25%-off promotion.
candidates: Smartish Gripmunk with MagSafe + MagSafe wallet

findings.label: Apple's rule for cases that hold cards when charging on MagSafe
findings.value: Remove cards, badges, passports and key fobs before charging, or make sure they aren't between the back of the device and the charger
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Quotes: "Don't place credit cards, security badges, passports, or key fobs between your iPhone and MagSafe Charger, because this might damage magnetic strips or RFID chips in those items." "If you have a case that holds any of these sensitive items, remove them before charging or make sure that they aren't between the back of your device and the charger." This page isn't among ChatGPT's results; it cited the Accessory Design Guidelines PDF instead.

findings.label: Wireless / MagSafe charging with the case on
findings.note: Quotes: "Wingmate cannot charge wirelessly or with MagSafe while the case is on; cable charging works with the case installed." "The ring does not enable wireless charging through Wingmate." Its MagSafe-ring add-on is for non-charging grips and stands only.

findings.label: Card capacity
findings.value: 3 cards + cash, or up to 4 slim cards without cash
findings.note: Quote: "Wingmate holds 3 cards plus cash, or up to 4 slim cards without cash, depending on thickness."

findings.value: "MagSafe & Qi2 charging compatible"; neodymium magnets with 800-1100 gf force when paired with Apple-certified accessories
findings.note: The page doesn't say whether charging works with cards inside or the cover closed, and has no FAQ on it. The 'wireless charging works through the case' line on the page is an AI-generated review summary, not a maker claim.

findings.label: Drop claim (maker)
findings.note: Quote: "protects against drops up to 8 feet". Raised edge above the screen: 0.85 mm at the bottom, 1.0 mm along the sides and top.
